record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Is the group ring of a right-orderable group embeddable in a Skew field?

evidence.quote: 2.11∗ . (A. I. Malcev [83] Problem 1.6) Is the group ring of a right orderable group embeddable in a Skew field?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called right-orderable if there exists a total order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a,b,c \in G$. For a field $K$, the group ring $K[G]$ is the $K$-algebra with basis $G$ and multiplication extended $K$-bilinearly from the group operation. A skew field (division ring) is an associative ring with $1 \ne 0$ in which every nonzero element has a two-sided multiplicative inverse. An embedding of $K[G]$ into a skew field $D$ is an injective ring homomorphism $K[G] \hookrightarrow D$.

Question: Does there exist, for every right-orderable group $G$ and every field $K$, a skew field $D$ and an injective ring homomorphism $K[G] \hookrightarrow D$? Equivalently, is the group ring of every right-orderable group embeddable in some skew field?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, originally posed by A. I. Malcev, asks whether the group ring of a right-orderable group embeds into a skew field. While Malcev and Neumann established the result for two-sided orderable groups, the right-orderable case remains open. Recent work (e.g., on Malcev–Neumann series rings) addresses related embedding questions but does not resolve the general problem.
